import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns

# Load the data from csv file
data = pd.read_csv('data/cameras.csv')

# Convert has_video_4k to categorical variable
data['has_video_4k'] = pd.Categorical(data['has_video_4k'], categories=[0, 1], ordered=True)

# Create a bar chart to compare the number of cameras with and without 4K video capabilities
plt.figure(figsize=(8, 6))
sns.countplot(x='has_video_4k', data=data)
plt.title('Number of Cameras with and without 4K Video Capabilities')
plt.xlabel('4K Video Capability')
plt.ylabel('Count')
plt.legend(title='4K Video Capability')
plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)

# Create a histogram to display the distribution of camera prices
plt.figure(figsize=(8, 6))
sns.histplot(data['price_usd'], bins=30, kde=True)
plt.title('Distribution of Camera Prices')
plt.xlabel('Price (USD)')
plt.ylabel('Frequency')
plt.xscale('log')
plt.savefig('prices.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)

# Create a box plot to compare the megapixels of cameras with different sensor types
plt.figure(figsize=(8, 6))
sns.boxplot(x='sensor_type', y='megapixels', data=data)
plt.title('Comparison of Megapixels by Sensor Type')
plt.xlabel('Sensor Type')
plt.ylabel('Megapixels')
plt.savefig('megapixels.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)
